NLPDataProcessor2.process_data:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Normalizes a list of strings into a list of word-token lists by lowercasing each string, removing all non-ASCII-letter and non-whitespace characters via regex, and splitting the result into individual word tokens." process_data]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> string_list </REF>: list[str] "A list of input strings to be cleaned and tokenized"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> words_list </REF>: list[list[str]] "A list of lists where each inner list contains the lowercase ASCII-letter word tokens extracted from the corresponding input string"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize an empty list named words_list to accumulate per-string token lists RESULT words_list]
            [COMMAND For each string in string_list, iterate once per element in order with no early exit RESULT string]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, convert string to lowercase and apply regex substitution to remove every character that is not an ASCII letter (a-z, A-Z) or whitespace; assign the result to processed_string RESULT processed_string]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, split processed_string on any whitespace sequence, discarding leading and trailing whitespace and collapsing internal runs, producing a list of lowercase letter-only word tokens; assign the result to words RESULT words]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, append words as a single element to words_list so that words_list[i] corresponds to string_list[i] RESULT words_list]
            [COMMAND After the loop completes all iterations, return words_list RESULT words_list]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NLPDataProcessor2.calculate_word_frequen:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Aggregates word counts from a list of word collections, then returns a dict of the top 5 most frequent words sorted in descending order of frequency." calculate_word_frequency]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> words_list </REF>: list "A list of iterables (e.g., lists or strings), each containing words whose frequencies are to be counted"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> top_5_word_frequency </REF>: dict "A dict of at most 5 entries mapping each top word (string) to its frequency count (int), ordered from highest to lowest frequency"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize an empty Counter named word_frequency RESULT word_frequency]
            [COMMAND For each element 'words' in words_list, call word_frequency.update(words) to accumulate counts from that element into word_frequency RESULT word_frequency]
            [COMMAND Sort all items in word_frequency by their count value (index 1 of each item tuple) in descending order, then reconstruct as a plain dict preserving that sorted insertion order, assigned to sorted_word_frequency RESULT sorted_word_frequency]
            [COMMAND Slice the first 5 items from sorted_word_frequency.items(), convert to a list, then reconstruct as a plain dict assigned to top_5_word_frequency; if sorted_word_frequency has fewer than 5 entries, all available entries are included without error RESULT top_5_word_frequency]
            [COMMAND Return top_5_word_frequency RESULT top_5_word_frequency]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: words_list is empty or all elements in words_list are empty iterables, so word_frequency accumulates no counts]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND word_frequency remains an empty Counter; sorted_word_frequency and top_5_word_frequency are both empty dicts; return the empty dict RESULT top_5_word_frequency]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: words_list has at least one non-empty element but the total number of distinct words across all elements is fewer than 5]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Proceed through all main_flow steps normally; the [:5] slice returns all available items without raising an error, so top_5_word_frequency contains fewer than 5 entries RESULT top_5_word_frequency]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: Multiple words share the same count value after aggregation]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND The sort is stable, so words tied in count retain their relative insertion order from word_frequency when building sorted_word_frequency, and the [:5] slice selects among tied words by that preserved order RESULT sorted_word_frequency]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NLPDataProcessor2.process:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Transforms a list of strings into a word frequency dictionary by delegating tokenization to process_data and frequency counting to calculate_word_frequency." process]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> string_list </REF>: list "A list of strings to be processed and analyzed for word frequency"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> word_frequency_dict </REF>: dict "A dictionary mapping each word to its occurrence count, derived from the processed string list"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call self.process_data with string_list as the argument and assign the result to words_list RESULT words_list]
            [COMMAND Call self.calculate_word_frequency with words_list as the argument and assign the result to word_frequency_dict RESULT word_frequency_dict]
            [COMMAND Return word_frequency_dict to the caller RESULT word_frequency_dict]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
